questions.q: What are the two common ways to render a KPI in Tableau, according to this lesson?
options: A shape-based indicator (like a checkmark/X assigned via a calculated field on the Shape mark) and a text-based number tile with conditional color
Only a pie chart and only a line chart
A KPI can only be built using a Gantt bar mark
KPIs require a third-party extension and cannot be built with native Tableau marks
questions.explain: The two approaches are shape-based indicators (a calculated field driving a Shape mark, like a green checkmark vs. red X) and text-based number tiles (a big aggregated number colored by a calculated field).

questions.q: In the calculated field example `IF SUM([Sales]) > 25000 THEN "Above Benchmark" ELSE "Below Benchmark" END`, what does this field control once placed on the Shape mark?
options: Which icon (e.g. checkmark vs. X) displays depending on whether sales exceed the benchmark
The exact color of every mark in the workbook
Which worksheet appears on the dashboard
The size of the dashboard canvas
questions.explain: The calculated field evaluates to one of two text outcomes, and each outcome is assigned its own shape (like a checkmark for above-benchmark, an X for below) via the Edit Shape dialog's KPI palette.

questions.q: How is a KPI header row typically assembled on a dashboard?
options: Several single-number worksheets placed inside one Horizontal container, evenly spaced, at the top of the dashboard
By exporting each KPI as a separate image and pasting them in
By building all KPIs on a single worksheet with 20 different axes
KPI headers cannot be built using containers
questions.explain: A KPI header is built from several minimal single-number worksheets dragged into one Horizontal container, then spaced evenly with Distribute Evenly.

questions.q: What is the 3-2-1 layout pattern this lesson recommends for an executive summary?
options: Three headline KPIs across the top, two trend/breakdown charts in the middle, and one detail area at the bottom
Three dashboards, two workbooks, one data source
Three filters, two parameters, one calculated field
It refers to three colors, two fonts, and one logo
questions.explain: 3-2-1 means three headline KPIs at the top, two supporting charts in the middle, and one detail/drill-down area at the bottom — a reusable structuring pattern, not a rigid rule.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against putting every available number into an executive summary section?
options: Because an executive summary that shows everything shows nothing — the goal is picking 5-10 KPIs that map directly to real business questions
Because Tableau has a hard technical limit of exactly 3 KPIs per dashboard
Because additional KPIs slow down Tableau Public specifically, but not Desktop
Because executive summaries are not allowed to contain any numbers at all
questions.explain: The point of an executive summary is ruthless prioritization — a handful of KPIs tied to real business questions, not a dump of every number the data contains, which defeats the purpose of a summary.
